title: CORTICAL DYSPLASIA, COMPLEX, WITH OTHER BRAIN MALFORMATIONS 17

intro.text: This entry describes complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations-17 (CDCBM17). I cannot reliably recall the specific causative gene, the inheritance pattern, or the primary reports for this subtype, so they are not stated here.

checks.claim: Complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations-17 (CDCBM17) is a subtype of complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract never mentions CDCBM or CDCBM17. It describes a 'novel disorder of cortical development' caused by DMRTA2 but does not classify it as a CDCBM subtype.

paragraphs.text: Complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations (CDCBM) is a group of neurodevelopmental disorders. They are defined by malformations of cortical development, such as lissencephaly/pachygyria, polymicrogyria-like cortical dysplasia, simplified gyral pattern, or heterotopia. These occur together with other brain malformations, such as abnormalities of the basal ganglia, corpus callosum, brainstem, and cerebellum. Affected individuals usually have developmental delay, intellectual disability, and often seizures and motor abnormalities. Most CDCBM forms are caused by mutations in genes that encode tubulins or microtubule-associated motor proteins.

checks.claim: Complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations (CDCBM) is a group of neurodevelopmental disorders.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention or define CDCBM. It describes lissencephaly as a group of cortical brain malformations, not CDCBM.

checks.claim: CDCBM is defined by malformations of cortical development, such as lissencephaly/pachygyria, polymicrogyria-like cortical dysplasia, simplified gyral pattern, or heterotopia.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not define CDCBM. It mentions lissencephaly and pachygyria only for lissencephaly in general and for this family, and it does not mention polymicrogyria, simplified gyral pattern or heterotopia.

checks.claim: In CDCBM, the malformations of cortical development occur together with other brain malformations, such as abnormalities of the basal ganglia, corpus callosum, brainstem, and cerebellum.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not characterise CDCBM. The only additional malformation it reports is agenesis of the corpus callosum in this family, and it does not mention the basal ganglia, brainstem or cerebellum.

checks.claim: Individuals with CDCBM usually have developmental delay.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not describe the clinical features of CDCBM in general, and it does not mention developmental delay.

checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention intellectual disability.

checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention seizures.

checks.claim: Individuals with CDCBM often have motor abnormalities.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention motor abnormalities.

checks.claim: Most forms of CDCBM are caused by mutations in genes that encode tubulins or microtubule-associated motor proteins.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention tubulins or microtubule-associated motor proteins as causes of CDCBM.

paragraphs.text: Complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations is genetically heterogeneous. Earlier forms include CDCBM1, caused by mutation in the TUBB3 gene; CDCBM2, caused by mutation in KIF5C; and CDCBM3, caused by mutation in KIF2A. CDCBM4 is caused by mutation in TUBG1 and CDCBM5 by mutation in TUBB2A.
